action_items.item: Add a pre-deploy or post-deploy smoke check that every dependency address in the production values (including the summary cache) accepts connections, and halt the rollout on failure.
Alert on sustained cache connection failures and cache hit ratio collapse for io-shop, and fix the HighLatency alert description so it matches the series it evaluates.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers saw slow account pages from {began} to {recovered}. The latency series the alert watches went from {series_before} to {series_while_broken} on average, peaking at {series_at_worst}. Outright failures barely changed: the error rate went from {errors_before} to {errors_while_broken}.

Each account-page request tried to look up its summary in the cache, failed, and only then fell back. The failed attempts added the delay. The logs show the cache lookup failing with connection refused for the whole broken window.

The cache lookups were refused because the service was now pointed at a cache address where nothing accepted connections. The cache service itself was healthy at its correct address, according to the Investigator's reading.

The address was changed by the deploy at {began}, the only production change near the onset. The incident began the same minute and every replica was on the new revision. Rolling back that deployment restored baseline.
The evidence stops here. The record does not show why a deploy with an unreachable cache address was able to roll out to all replicas without being stopped.

contributing_factors.factor: The deploy pipeline did not check that the configured cache address was reachable before or during rollout, so a bad value reached every replica.

Detection relied on a latency alert that fired after the onset ({alert_raised} against {began}). The cache connection-refused errors in the logs were not themselves alerting, and the alert's description talked about error rate while the series was latency.
The durable fix to the configuration was still only a draft pull request, so the underlying change remains unresolved until it is reviewed and merged.

input.executive_summary: Shoppers using the io-shop account pages saw slow responses for {duration}, starting at {began}. Latency rose from about {series_before} to about {series_while_broken} on average, peaking at {series_at_worst}. Few requests failed outright: the error rate moved from {errors_before} to {errors_while_broken}, peaking at {errors_at_worst}. The cause was a configuration change in a deploy that pointed the service at the wrong address for its summary cache. Argus rolled the deployment back, the metrics returned to baseline, and the incident was closed after {held} of response. A draft pull request with a proper fix has been proposed and still needs review.

got_lucky: The service fell back when the cache failed, so the effect was slowness rather than a large rise in errors.
went_well: Argus tied the onset to the deploy and the cache connection-refused log line within seconds and rolled back at once.
The rollback was verified against the metrics before the incident was marked mitigated.
A draft fix pull request was proposed right after mitigation.
went_wrong: A configuration change that made a dependency unreachable passed through to every replica unchecked.
The alert fired after the onset and its description did not match what it measured.

input.root_cause: The production deploy at {began} (P2) shipped a changed cache address in the io-shop production values, pointing the summary cache at a port where nothing was listening. Every cache lookup was refused, and each account-page request wasted time on the failed connection before falling back, so pages became much slower. Nothing in the deploy path checked that the cache was reachable.
